**Finding: compliant** — no MFN obligation burdens us.

I searched the whole agreement for MFN-style language ("most favoured nation", "no less favourable", "favourable/favorable", "best", "price", "other customers", "third part") and checked both planner candidates:

- **§ 11 (Fees)** contains only a payment obligation: *"Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule..."* — no pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** covers only time-of-essence and notices.
- The only "third party" references are in the use restrictions, confidentiality, and assignment clauses — none create a matching or parity obligation.

Sparkling is therefore under no obligation to extend Garman terms no less favourable than those given to others, or to match third-party offers. That sits at the **preferred position** (no MFN on Customer), so no redline was proposed. Worth noting for commercial context only: the agreement also contains no Vendor-granted MFN in our favour, which would have been welcome but is not something this rule requires us to raise.
